newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Portugal seeks more active EU role.
newsitem.headline: Portugal seeks more active EU role.

text.p: Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio, in his first official visit to the European Commission, said on Thursday Lisbon wanted a more active European role.
"I do not like to see Portugal as the 'good pupil' (of the European Union); I like to see Portugal as a full partner in European construction," he told a news conference after meeting the Commission.
European Economic Affairs Yves-Thibault de Silguy, asked recently about the chances of Portugal qualifying for the start of the EU's single currency, said : "good pupil; must continue".

Portugal, which joined the EU in 1986, is rarely seen taking initiatives or creating any specific problems in the 15-nation bloc except when particular interests such as fisheries or the fate of its once, huge colonial empire, are at stake.

Recently, however, it took the lead by putting forward a proposal for greater flexibility in EU affairs that would allow groups of countries, not the whole bloc, to progress in certain areas such as foreign affairs.

Portugal has also contributed to bringing the attention of the international community to the violation of human rights in the Indonesian-occupied territory of East Timor, which was formerly under Portuguese rule.

"There is this idea that we only care about matters which affect us; it's not like this," said Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaima Gama, who is accompanying Sampaio on his four-day visit ending on Friday.
